ASCII-art diagram titled "One token by telegraph", showing how one transformer layer would be computed by a fictional civilisation. At the top, a skyline drawing depicts the Capital — a city of 1,000,000 core scribes — connected by roughly 300 km of telegraph wire (100 bits per second, signals at 0.7c) to the Towns, where 10,000,000 more scribes work.
Below the skyline is a timeline for computing one layer (layer k of 120, processed strictly in order), with two parallel columns: the Capital (one million scribes, 10 km wide) and the Towns (ten million scribes, 300 km out). The timeline reads:
Hour 0.0: the Capital begins self-attention. This happens in the core only, because every desk may need to read the whole token census. Half the city is on duty at any time, in two 12-hour shifts. It takes 9.4 hours of arithmetic plus 1.8 hours of keying messages across the city's own wires, finishing at hour 11.3.
Hour 11.3: the Capital transmits the MLP inputs for layer k to the Towns — 327 kilobits, about 0.9 hours of keying. The 300 km of light-lag adds only 1.4 milliseconds.
Hour 12.2: both sides compute the MLP feed-forward in step. The Towns' ten million desks each work on their own slice, no town consulting another; the Capital's on-duty half joins with its own share. This takes 0.9 hours.
Hour 13.0: the Towns key the MLP outputs back to the Capital — another 327 kilobits, 0.9 hours.
